newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chase CEO sees drawbacks, can't exclude Lehman buy.
newsitem.headline: Chase CEO sees drawbacks, can't exclude Lehman buy.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp chairman and chief executive Walter Shipley said on Monday he would not rule out Chase acquiring a company like Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc, but highlighted drawbacks to such a deal.
Asked whether Chase would consider acquiring a company such as Lehman Brothers, Shipley told Reuters Financial Television:
"We have said our strategy has been to build our own equity competency and underwriting competency, and to date that has been our strategy.

"In a fast-changing world such as we are in, we don't rule it out. But our business is a people business, and particularly the investment banking side, so you have to be very sure that the cultural integration and fit will work."
An acquisition like this carried a "much higher risk of losing staff who were unhappy with a combined situation", Shipley said.
"We also think the cultural fit is better by selecting individuals that we might need to complement our skills and use them as a core of competency to build their own talent."
